What it takes off you

None of it is hard. It is just spread across everything you own.

Not one of these is difficult, which is exactly why they pile up. Every add-on named here is one you can read today, under the name it actually has.

  • “When are you free Thursday?”

    You open the calendar to answer the mail, then go back to the mail. Your agent reads both and hands you the reply.

    Find a Timeneeds your calendar
  • “Did they ever write back?”

    You cannot answer that without scrolling your sent mail. Each morning it says who owes you one, and stays quiet when nothing moved.

    Reply Watchneeds your mail
  • “Did I say I would send that?”

    Promises live in sent mail, which is where they go to be forgotten. It re-reads yours and tells you what is due.

    Commitment Sweepneeds your mail
  • “What is actually charging me?”

    A card, a bank app, and a folder of confirmation emails. It keeps one list with real dates, including the ones renewing in the dark.

    Bills & Subscriptions
  • “Which step was I on?”

    Visas, permits, benefits, enrolment. No map, and you start from the top every time. It holds the step, the missing documents, and what comes next.

    Paperwork
  • “What did the doctor say?”

    Gone by the time you reach the car park. Tell it once and it keeps a dated record, what changed, and your questions for next time.

    Health Record

Six of a hundred and fifty-one, and they were picked for having nothing to do with each other. The calendar, the school mail, what is arriving in the post, the birthdays, the prescriptions, dinner and the trip are the same shape: small, spread out, and yours to stop doing.

And the rows that are still blank.

  • Buying it, booking it, paying itArchie cannot spend money or buy anything. It finds the flight and holds the return window; the card stays yours.
  • Your bank, read directlyBills & Subscriptions, Money In & Out and Savings Goals keep the list you give them, and connect to no bank.
  • A job huntNothing on the shelf does this yet. Commission it, and it joins the marketplace, included with Archie for everyone after you.

Adding rows is not free. Add-ons with routines run on their own schedule, and those runs are a real part of a heavy month’s AI bill before you have typed anything. What that costs, measured →

Where your words go

Your conversations go to your AI provider. Not to us.

Your computerArchie, your files, your keys
direct, on your own account
Your AI provideryour pick of 7, switch any time

Otian’s servers hold your email address and plan, plus the operational records on our trust page. Never a conversation. One exception: the free starter credits, and the plan with the AI included, reach Anthropic through a server of ours. We keep none of it, and connecting your own account stops it.

  • Keys in your computer’s password store
  • We never hold your conversations
  • Your own AI account, your own key
  • No analytics service in the app
  • Add-ons are text, not code
  • Nothing connects until you connect it
